sections.overview: The bearded pygmy chameleon is a tiny, short-tailed chameleon of the forests of eastern Tanzania and south-eastern Kenya. It lives close to the ground, among leaf litter and low bushes. Its scientific name means short-tailed.
sections.identification: Adults are around 8 cm long. The sources consulted do not publish a dependable adult body mass or sex-specific length range, so neither is estimated here. A very small chameleon, about 8 cm long, named for its scaly throat with two chin lobes. It can change colour among brown, yellow, green, orange and black, to show stress or attract a mate. Sleeping in the open, it can flatten its body and show a side stripe that looks like a dead leaf.
sections.habitat: It lives in lowland forest of eastern Tanzania and south-eastern Kenya, including submontane and coastal forest, on the leafy forest floor and in low bushes. The Rondo Plateau in Tanzania is one confirmed locality, and the type locality is Derema in the Usambara Mountains.
sections.diet: It eats small insects, which it hunts in the leaf litter of the forest floor and in low shrubs.
sections.behavior: It is usually active during the day and clings to the twigs and leaves of low bushes, hunting close to the ground. Beyond this, little about its daily life is documented in the sources consulted.
sections.reproduction: The Reptile Database lists the species as egg-laying. Clutch size, incubation time and age at maturity are not given in the sources consulted, so they are left out here.
sections.ecology: Its dead-leaf look helps it escape the notice of predators, and it depends on the rich leafy understorey of healthy evergreen forest, where it hunts small insects.
sections.conservation: It is classed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List according to a conservation charity and the Reptile Database. Habitat loss and deforestation are the main threats: its estimated range covers about 163,800 square kilometres, but forest makes up less than a tenth of that area.
